segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Hello?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Oh, hello. Is that Julie Davison?

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: This is Greg Preston from the Employment Agency. We met last week when you came in to enquire about office work.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Oh, that’s right.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Now we’ve just had some details come in of a job which might interest you.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: So this is a position for a receptionist – I believe you’ve done that sort of work before?

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Yes, I have, I worked in a sports centre for a couple of years before I got married and had the children.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Right. Well, this job’s in Fordham, so not too far away for you, and it’s at the medical centre there.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: OK. So where exactly is that?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: It’s quite near the station, on Chastons Road.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Sorry?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Chastons Road- that’s C-H-A-S-T-O-N-S.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: OK, thanks. So what would the work involve? Dealing with enquiries from patients?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Yes, and you’d also be involved in making appointments, whether face to face or on the phone. And rescheduling them if necessary.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Fine, that shouldn’t be a problem.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: And another of your duties would be keeping the centre’s database up-to-date. Then you might have other general administrative duties as well, but those would be the main ones.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Now when the details came in, I immediately thought of you because one thing they do require is someone with experience, and you did mention your work at the sports centre when you came in to see us.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Yes, in fact I enjoyed that job. Is there anything else they’re looking for?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Well, they say it’s quite a high-pressure environment, they’re always very busy, and patients are often under stress, so they want someone who can cope with that and stay calm, and at the same time be confident when interacting with the public.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Well, after dealing with three children all under five, I reckon I can cope with that.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: I’m sure you can.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: And then another thing they mention is that they’re looking for someone with good IT skills ...

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Not a problem.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: So you’d be interested in following this up?

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Sure. When would it start?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Well, they’re looking for someone from the beginning of next month, but I should tell you that this isn’t a permanent job, it’s temporary, so the contract would be just to the end of September. But they do say that there could be further opportunities after that.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: OK. And what would the hours be?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Well, they want someone who can start at a quarter to eight in the morning could you manage that?

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Yes, my husband would have to get the kids up and off to my mother’s – she’s going to be looking after them while I’m at work. What time would I finish

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: One fifteen.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: That should work out all right. I can pick the kids up on my way home, and then I’ll have the afternoon with them. Oh, one thing ... is there parking available for staff at the centre?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Yes, there is. and it’s also on a bus route.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Right. Well, I expect I’ll have the car but it’s good to know that. OK, so where do I go from here?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Well, if you’re happy for me to do so, I’ll forward your CV and references, and then the best thing would probably be for you to phone them so they can arrange for an interview.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Great. Well thank you very much.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: You’re welcome. Bye now.

segments.speaker: JULIE
segments.en: Bye.
